sources.title: Index Chemicus — Keynes MS.30/1 (catalogue title: Quomodo Metalla generantur et corrumpuntur in venis)
sources.date_note: Newton manuscript; precise composition date not established in this pass. Electronic edition/catalogue inspected 2026-09-27.
sources.version: ALCH00200 normalized scholarly transcription; Index Chemicus Ordinatus cross-checked
sources.sections_read: Catalogue introduction; Adrop entry (web lines 409–411); Aqua vitae/viridis (676–686); Duenech (1566–1580); Saturnus/aqua fortis passage (2335–2349); selected Mercurius entries in reordered index.
sources.reading_depth: Selected catalogue and primary Latin entries, interpreted narrowly; no manuscript-image collation or complete index reading.
sources.provenance: Newton autograph literature index, scholarly transcription at Indiana University; cited older authorities are not Newton's experimental confirmations.
sources.claim_category: Historical primary compilation and context-dependent terminology
sources.supports: The same name can index different materials or symbolic roles. Adrop connects lead/Saturn with several additional readings; Saturn elsewhere appears as aqua fortis.
sources.does_not_support: A universal cipher, a modern formula for every term, elemental transmutation, or a verified identity of an actual sample.
sources.unresolved: Date and ambiguous glyphs require manuscript collation; chemical reconstruction requires passage-specific material analysis.

sources.reading_depth: Selected complete guide prose and relevant symbol groups.

sources.title: Alchemical Glossary — The Chymistry of Isaac Newton
sources.sections_read: Aqua fortis, aqua vitae, arsenic, butter of antimony, rectification, regulus and regulus martis; terminology only.
sources.reading_depth: Selected entries; preparation details deliberately not reproduced.
sources.provenance: Scholarly historical glossary, supplying modern reconstructions rather than measured compositions.
sources.supports: Arsenic may denote arsenic trioxide; regulus commonly denotes metallic antimony or an alloy. A historical material word need not name a pure element.
sources.does_not_support: An assay result for Newton's material, universal formula assignments, or safe historical-recipe instructions.
sources.unresolved: Impurity, oxidation state, phase and usage vary with context.

sources.title: Pauli to C. G. Jung: letters of 23 December 1947, 16 June 1948 and 7 November 1948
sources.date_note: Three letters, through 1948-11-07; reproduced from C. A. Meier ed. (1992), pp.36–39.

sources.provenance: ETH-hosted reproduction of edited primary letters, not autograph images.

sources.does_not_support: Controlled evidence of psychic effects, physical radioactivity in dreams, or quantum observer claims about consciousness.
